name: Mattaniah
overview: Mattaniah is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Zattu who had married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:27. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His mention highlights a specific instance of intermarriage addressed in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattaniah means 'gift of YHWH,' indicating a theophoric name that reflects a dedication or connection to the LORD. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaning that honors the divine.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Mattaniah as a descendant of Zattu, establishing a direct genealogical link. Beyond this relationship, no further family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mattaniah’s significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the returning exiles concerning intermarriage with foreign wives. His mention in Ezra 10:27 underscores the community's effort to uphold covenantal purity and faithfulness to God’s commands during the restoration period. Through this, Mattaniah exemplifies the broader struggle to maintain holiness and obedience in the post-exilic era.
